title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model error. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems is alleged to have used them for a purpose they were not authorised for: tracking and surveilling a woman without her consent. The systems named, a Flock camera system, a tag reader system and the Georgia Crime Information Center database, were built and provisioned for police work, and the alleged failure is that they were turned to a personal end by someone holding the credentials to query them.

The point of exposure is the query itself. Access controls that grant a deputy the ability to look up plates or database records do not, on their own, distinguish a lawful lookup from an unlawful one, so detection depends on audit trails, anomaly review or a report from the person affected. The indictment followed a GBI investigation, which is the kind of after-the-fact review that establishes what was queried and when.

The charges are allegations. An indictment is not a conviction, and the counts of oath violation, computer invasion of privacy, prohibited use of captured license plate data and stalking have not been proven. Rozar was terminated when the investigation began and released on bond the day of his arrest, and his arraignment is scheduled for May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A Coffee County grand jury indicted former sheriff's deputy Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege that between April 10 and May 1, 2024, Rozar misused the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons, including tracking and surveilling a woman without her consent. The GBI investigated, and Rozar was terminated when the investigation began.

Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. The woman at the center of the allegations spoke anonymously to WALB, saying she waited two years for the investigation and hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
